what.text: Mechano growth factor (MGF) is the name given to a form of insulin-like growth factor 1 (IGF-1) that muscle makes after mechanical stress. In people it comes from a splice variant called IGF-1Ec. The “MGF peptide” studied in labs is a synthetic chain of 24 amino acids from the end (E-domain) of this form.

what.text: PEG-MGF is MGF with polyethylene glycol (PEG) attached. It is not an official drug name. No published study of PEG-MGF itself was found.

what.text: In a lab study, the short MGF peptide and a stabilized version did not switch on the IGF-1 receptor at all. A longer, “full-length” MGF did, though it needed about nine times the concentration of IGF-1.

src.label: Janssen JA, et al. PLoS One 2016

what.text: There are no published studies of PEG-MGF in people or animals. Doping labs have found MGF variants in seized vials.

research.text: No published human studies found as of November 1, 2026. FDA has not identified any human exposure data on PEG-MGF by any route. A 2026 review of these peptides likewise found no peer-reviewed human studies.

research.title: A “full-length MGF” product offered to athletes

facts.v: laboratory analysis of a product obtained from illicit channels
what protein the product contained, and whether doping tests can detect it

research.found: The product held a protein close to IGF-1Ec, with a changed end. Adapted routine doping tests could detect it. MGF has been treated as prohibited by WADA since 2005.

facts.v: laboratory analysis of seized vials and test-tube breakdown in plasma
identity and stability, to build doping tests

research.found: One vial held an MGF variant (MGF R23H) that was stable in plasma and should be detectable in urine.

src.label: Cox HD, et al. Drug Test Anal 2017

research.title: Does MGF switch on the IGF-1 receptor?

facts.v: activation of the IGF-1 and insulin receptors by full-length MGF, short MGF peptides and IGF-1

research.found: Full-length MGF switched on the IGF-1 receptor at high concentrations. The short MGF peptides did not. Effects in the body were not tested.

us.text: PEG-MGF is not FDA approved for any use. FDA lists it on its Category 2 page (bulk drug substances that may present significant safety risks), among nominations that were later withdrawn, and says it has found no human exposure data. As of November 1, 2026.

items.text: FDA lists “Mechano growth factor pegylated (PEG-MGF)” among nominations that were withdrawn. FDA says compounded PEG-MGF “may pose significant risk for immunogenicity for certain routes of administration and may have complexities with regard to peptide-related impurities and API characterization. FDA has not identified any human exposure data on drug products containing PEG-MGF administered via any route of administration.”

after.text: Mechano growth factors are prohibited at all times under class S2.3 (growth factors and growth factor modulators) of the 2026 Prohibited List, which names “Mechano growth factors (MGFs).” PEG-MGF is not named separately. S2 substances are not “specified substances.” The 2027 list keeps the entry.

side.text: Nothing is known about PEG-MGF’s side effects in people. FDA says it lacks important information on any safety issues, including whether it would cause harm.
